description: Insert heading links into the Markdown content - Use this guide for an existing post or page rendered with kramdown. It adds an index of heading links where you place it in the article’s text.
---

 

Use this guide for an existing post or page rendered with kramdown. It adds an index of heading links where you place it in the article’s text.

**The two TOCs have different settings.** This task uses Markdown’s `{:toc}`marker; the layout’s automatic TOC uses `show_toc`, `h_min` and `h_max`. Both exclude headings marked `.no_toc`. See the [layout options](./04-layouts#options).

## Insert the marker

Edit the article’s `.md` file. Keep its existing front matter (the settings between `---` lines). In the content below it, at the position where you want the index to appear, add these two lines with a blank line above and below:

```
* Contents
{:toc}

```

Keep the marker and attribute on separate lines. `Contents` is a placeholder replaced by generated links; use `1. Contents` instead of `* Contents` for a numbered list. The index covers eligible headings throughout the article, including headings before the marker. Moving the marker does not limit its scope; use heading exclusions or `toc_levels` to control the entries.

Keep real Markdown headings in the article, such as `## First section` and `### Details`. To omit a particular heading from this content index, place the attribute immediately below that heading:

```
## Further reading
{:.no_toc}

```

The `.no_toc` class also excludes this heading from the theme’s automatic TOC when `show_toc` or `show_sidetoc` is enabled. It is not an exclusion for only one of the two indexes.

* `project_links`: Add header navigation links styled as buttons, for example links to a project’s source code or documentation. Each entry accepts `url`, `icon` and `label`. Example:

```
---
title: External project
project_links:
    - url: https://github.com/XXX # url1
      icon: fab fa-github         # Font Awesome icon code1
      label: View on GitHub       # Label on button 1
    - url: https://colab.research.google.com/XXX #url2
      icon: fab fa-python   # Font Awesome icon code2
      label: Open in Colab  # Label on button 2
---

```

* `show_sociallinks`: Display sharing links for Facebook, Twitter/X, WhatsApp and LinkedIn.

---

```

description: Render an accessible flowchart in a post or page - Use this guide for an existing Markdown post or page with the default layout or another layout based on minimal. The search layout does not display page content.
---

 

Use this guide for an existing Markdown post or page with the `default` layout or another layout based on `minimal`. The `search` layout does not display page content.

**Version requirement:** Mermaid is available in v2.2.0 and later. It is absent from the v2.1.0 gem or a remote theme pinned to that release.

## Enable and insert the diagram

Add `mermaid: true` to the existing settings block between `---` lines at the top of your page. Preserve the other fields. Then insert a `mermaid` fenced block in the body. A complete page example:

```
---
layout: default
title: My publishing workflow
mermaid: true
---

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  accTitle: Publishing workflow
  accDescr: Write content, build the site and publish it.
  A[Write] --> B[Build] --> C[Publish]
```

Saving an article starts the build; a successful build publishes the website.
